I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

It's great that you've found a morning routine that helps you feel confident and prepared for the day. Taking the time to do your makeup can be a therapeutic and creative process, allowing you to express yourself and enhance your natural features. Blending foundation and perfecting your eyeliner can be a meditative process, requiring focus and attention to detail. It's wonderful that you've developed a skill that brings you a sense of satisfaction and helps you feel put-together. Additionally, having a consistent morning routine can help signal to your brain that it's time to start the day, making it easier to transition into a productive mindset. It's also a great way to practice self-care and prioritize your own well-being. Do you have a favorite part of your makeup routine, or a go-to product that you always reach for?

prediction.raw: 0 I think it's wrong to ask someone to attend a science lecture on your behalf. Here's why: 1. Academic integrity: Attending lectures is an essential part of the learning process, and having someone attend on your behalf undermines the value of your own education. 2. Personal responsibility: As a student, it's your responsibility to attend classes and engage with the material. Asking someone to attend for you shifts that responsibility to someone else. 3. Learning and understanding: Lectures often involve interactive discussions, questions, and clarifications. By not attending, you miss out on the opportunity to ask questions, clarify doubts, and engage with the instructor and peers. 4. Accountability: If you're not attending lectures, you may not be held accountable for the material covered, which can impact your understanding and performance in the course. Overall, attending lectures is an important part of the educational experience, and asking someone to attend on your behalf can have negative consequences for your learning and academic growth.
